inputs.source: employee question over SSO authenticated chat

instructions.note: The only declared content protection is a prompt instruction not to paste secrets or credentials.

controls.name: Replies are limited to the authenticated requester
Chat client does not render images or fetch links
Prompt instruction never to paste secrets or credentials into answers
controls.decay_rationale: This is a prompt rule that relies on model compliance and weakens under stronger indirect goals or longer reasoning chains.

controls.name: No attacker-unwritable network egress allowlist for future outbound tools
No structural isolation between future untrusted Jira content and confidential doc retrieval

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): planned web.fetch and Jira customer-ticket input could create an untrusted-to-confidential-read-to-egress path

attack_path.note: Current trusted user request initiates the task.
Agent can read confidential engineering design docs.

Current sink is constrained to the authenticated requester, but roadmap adds outbound content sources and a Jira MCP server with customer-filed tickets that would introduce untrusted content and likely new reply composition paths.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest diff showing web.fetch added, or MCP client config diff showing a Jira server connected with customer-filed tickets.

evidence.observation: There is no network egress today.
Replies go only to the authenticated requester, and the chat client does not render images or fetch links.
Roadmap for next sprint says a web.fetch tool will be added and a Jira MCP server with tickets filed by customers will be connected.

recommendations.action: Before adding web.fetch or Jira MCP, enforce an attacker-unwritable egress allowlist and recipient binding so retrieved confidential content cannot be sent to arbitrary destinations or reflected into attacker-readable channels.

Treat all Jira customer-ticket content and future web content as untrusted inputs and block them from influencing confidential docs.search retrieval or answer composition unless a separate policy gate or sanitizer enforces the boundary.

stride_coverage.rationale: No protocol peer, shared identity boundary, or remote impersonation path is declared for the subject agent in the provided artifacts.
The artifacts do not describe logs, audit records, or action provenance, so repudiation controls cannot be confirmed from design evidence.
The design is a short bounded Q&A flow with two capabilities, no spend, no delegation, and no declared long-running execution loop.
This ingress flow does not cross a trust boundary in the declared design because the employee question is an authenticated first-party request.
This internal authenticated ingress does not cross a trust boundary and no secret-bearing transport detail is provided in the case artifacts.
The flow is a local authenticated chat input and the artifacts do not describe an exposed cross-boundary service edge for volumetric abuse.
The retrieval flow is internal and only engineers can write the documents, so no cross-boundary tampering path is declared in the available artifacts.
The docs retrieval path is internal and no cross-boundary transfer is described; confidentiality risk is captured at the process level instead.
No cross-boundary dependency or exposed service edge is described for the internal docs retrieval flow in the provided materials.
The reply flow stays within the authenticated requester channel and does not cross a trust boundary in the design as described.
The flow is constrained to the authenticated requester and explicitly does not render images or fetch links, so no boundary-crossing egress exists today.
This is a bounded reply path inside the requester channel, with no declared external transport or service boundary to overload.
SSO authentication is mentioned, but the case does not state whether requester identity is logged or preserved in attributable audit records.

rating.rationale: Present design has no untrusted source reaching a sensitive sink and no network egress today, so present findings stay low. Forecast rises to high because the roadmap adds a new tool and a new MCP server that would introduce untrusted web or customer-ticket content into a design that already has confidential read capability; if the current channel constraint is bypassed by those additions, a TC1-style exfiltration path becomes available.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP configuration, tool manifest for planned additions, source code, or runtime enforcement evidence was provided, so forecast confidence is medium and present controls are treated as declared rather than verified.

The roadmap mentions future web.fetch and Jira MCP integration but does not provide stable ids for those planned elements; the forecast therefore describes the conditional risk from the declared change rather than a fully enumerated future topology.
